predictions.event: Los Angeles Kings @ New Jersey Devils
predictions.write_up: New Jersey have turned 33 goals for and 31 against into a 6-4-0 record, while Los Angeles limp in at 2-4-2 with only 20 goals in eight games and 29 conceded. That gap of better than a goal a night at the Prudential Center points one way: take the Devils on the money line, with the 3.61-2.69 projection explaining why the puck line is the riskier route. The official preview carries no injury note.

Boston arrive at 8-2-1 having conceded just 22 goals in eleven outings, the meanest defensive record on this slate, and they are scoring 3.82 a night. San Jose are 6-4-1 but have shipped 36 goals in the same number of games, and our 3.76-2.32 projection makes the Bruins on the money line the clear play. No absence was listed on the official game page when this was written.

Washington sit 5-4-0 with 30 goals scored and 29 conceded in nine games, numbers that read as ordinary until you set them against a Buffalo side leaking 3.60 a game and managing only 2.80. The Capitals' home ice tilts the projection to 3.64-2.85, so Washington on the money line is the selection. Nothing about availability appears on the official game centre for either club.

predictions.event: Vegas Golden Knights @ Columbus Blue Jackets
predictions.write_up: Vegas are 8-4-0 with 45 goals in twelve, Columbus 3-5-0 with only 19 scored in eight and 29 conceded, and the Golden Knights have the better of this on raw rates even before travel is considered. Our projection of 3.53-2.86 to the visitors makes Vegas the money-line call rather than the heavy puck line. The league's official page lists no scratches at the time of writing.

Edmonton are 8-1-1 and averaging 4.60 goals a game, the best attacking rate in the league's published summary, which is exactly the sort of number that travels badly for visiting goaltenders. Toronto counter at 6-4-2 with 43 goals in twelve, but concede 3.17 a night. Our 4.09-3.25 projection favours the Oilers to win, and the total has value over the posted number. No roster absence was published.

predictions.event: Tampa Bay Rays @ Milwaukee Brewers (World Series Game 1)
predictions.write_up: Milwaukee open the World Series at home off a 103-59 regular season in which they outscored opponents by 214 runs, the biggest margin of any club in the official standings. Tampa Bay were excellent in their own right at 98-64, but their plus-86 differential is less than half of it. Back the Brewers on the money line in game one; the run line is a stretch at a projected 4.76-4.01.

predictions.event: Tampa Bay Rays @ Milwaukee Brewers (World Series Game 2)
predictions.write_up: Game two keeps the series at American Family Field, where Milwaukee's run environment of 832 scored against 618 allowed over 162 games is worth roughly three quarters of a run a night over Tampa Bay. The Rays' pitching held opponents to 650 runs, so this stays a tight contest rather than a mismatch: Brewers to win is the selection, with under the posted total the sensible secondary angle.

predictions.event: Milwaukee Brewers @ Tampa Bay Rays (World Series Game 3)
predictions.write_up: The series switches to Tropicana Field and our price on Milwaukee shortens from -148 to -127 purely on venue. That is the honest size of home advantage here: Tampa Bay's 98-64 season and 650 runs allowed make them awkward at home, while Milwaukee still carry the stronger differential. Brewers on the money line remains the call for game three, but it is a thinner edge than in Wisconsin.

predictions.event: Milwaukee Brewers @ Tampa Bay Rays (World Series Game 4)
predictions.write_up: Game four is the first of this series where a Tampa Bay side that won 98 games could already be playing with the pressure of a deficit. Our numbers still read 4.39-4.35 to the home team on expected runs yet make Milwaukee a small favourite overall, because the Brewers' 832 runs scored is the best figure of any team in the captured standings. Brewers to win, narrowly.

predictions.event: Milwaukee Brewers @ Tampa Bay Rays (World Series Game 5)
predictions.write_up: Listed by the league as an if-necessary date, game five would see Milwaukee bidding to close out a series in St. Petersburg. The Brewers' 103-59 record and plus-214 differential justify a -127 price even on the road, and Tampa Bay's 736 runs scored is the lowest total among the four teams captured from the standings feed. Brewers to win if this one is played.

Dubai are 5-2 and shade this on both sides of the ball: 85.3 points for and 83.4 against, against a Paris side that has won once in six and is conceding 90.8. The hosts' projected 89.6-82.2 win makes them the two-way selection, and with both teams playing at pace the 172-point total is worth a look over rather than under.

predictions.event: Crvena Zvezda Meridianbet Belgrade v Maccabi Rapyd Tel Aviv
predictions.write_up: Crvena Zvezda have built a 4-3 record on defence, allowing just 76.0 points a game, the second-best figure in the standings after Fenerbahce. Maccabi have conceded 93.3 a game while winning twice in seven. A projected 88.1-79.9 in Belgrade makes the hosts the selection on the two-way line, and the eight-point handicap is priced almost as a coin flip for a reason.

predictions.event: FC Bayern Munich v FC Barcelona
Panathinaikos AKTOR Athens v Armani Olimpia Milan
predictions.write_up: Panathinaikos are 6-1 with 613 points scored and 517 conceded in seven rounds, a plus-96 differential that leads the competition, and they face a Milan side that has won once in seven while conceding 92.6 a game. Athens is a brutal place to arrive in that state. The hosts to win is close to a formality at our price; the 14.5-point handicap is where the real interest lies.

predictions.event: Valencia Basket v Fenerbahce Tarfin Istanbul
Kosner Baskonia Vitoria-Gasteiz v Real Madrid
Hapoel IBI Tel Aviv v Anadolu Efes Istanbul
predictions.write_up: Hapoel Tel Aviv are the highest-scoring team in the competition at 90.0 points a game, with 630 scored in seven rounds, and they are 5-2. Anadolu Efes are 3-4 and have the most neutral profile in the league, 581 for and 590 against. At -223 this sits inside the price band we are focused on: take Hapoel to win, with the 5.5-point handicap the alternative.

predictions.event: LDLC ASVEL Villeurbanne v Partizan Mozzart Bet Belgrade

predictions.write_up: Virtus Bologna's 4-3 record hides an even scoring profile - 606 for, 608 against - but Zalgiris arrive 2-4 with the lowest output in the competition at 81.7 points a game. Home advantage at PalaDozza is worth three points in our calculation and turns a near coin flip into a 67 per cent call. Virtus to win is the play at a price inside our focus range.

Port Moresby gives Papua New Guinea as loud a home advantage as exists in the sport and they opened with a 42-18 win over Lebanon. Samoa's 78-4 demolition of France is the louder scoreline, but a capped and shrunk one-match sample plus four points of home edge leaves this all but even: PNG by the barest margin, and the handicap of two points is the fairer bet.

England were beaten 30-12 by Tonga and need a response in Perth, a neutral venue where no home edge applies to either side. France were taken apart 78-4 by Samoa, the heaviest defeat of the tournament so far, and even with that differential capped at thirty points they remain the weaker team here. England to win, and the 62-point total looks low given France's defensive week.

New Zealand lost 24-22 to Australia in a World Cup opener they led late, then watched the Cook Islands ship 40 points to Fiji. Christchurch is a genuine home venue for the Kiwis and our projection of 30.8-18.2 reflects both the quality gap and the Cook Islands' defensive problems. New Zealand to win is the selection, with the 12.5-point handicap the better-value version of the same opinion.

This is the one row on the desk where the published numbers and conventional expectation part company. Australia's only World Cup result is a 24-22 win over New Zealand; Fiji's is a 40-12 dismantling of the Cook Islands, so on points differential alone Fiji grade out stronger even after shrinking a one-game sample. We publish Fiji as the price-implied side at Suncorp Stadium and flag it loudly rather than quietly overriding the data.

Gloucester and Bath arrive at Kingsholm with identical W,W,L runs over their last three, so this one rests almost entirely on venue. Five points of home advantage is enough to make Gloucester a 65 per cent call rather than a coin flip, which is why the selection is the hosts on the two-way line rather than the handicap. Neither club's line-up was posted on the official fixtures page.

predictions.event: Newcastle Red Bulls v Sale Sharks
predictions.write_up: Newcastle have lost each of their last three and host a Sale side that has won two of three, which flips the usual home calculus. Even after crediting the Red Bulls with five points of home advantage the numbers favour the visitors, so Sale to win is the pick at a price close to evens. The official page carried no availability update for either squad.

Leicester come in on L,W,W, Northampton on W,L,W - the same two wins in three, with the Tigers holding Welford Road. That is the entire edge, and at -186 the price says as much: a home win is the selection but this is a derby decided by inches rather than a mismatch, so the five-point handicap is the more honest expression of it.

Bristol take a W,W,L run into Ashton Gate against an Exeter side that has lost two of its last three and won only once. With the league table unreadable on the official site, form and venue are all we have, and both point the same way: Bristol to win, with the 8.5-point handicap representing the same view at a longer price. No team sheet had been published when this was written.

Harlequins arrive at the Stoop on a three-match losing run while Saracens have won two of their last three, and the two-point handicap in Saracens' favour is the cleanest way to express it. The straight win at -128 is the selection, though with no league table published on the official site this is a form-and-venue call and deliberately cautious.

Sloga Doboj won the first leg of this European Cup tie 38-26 away from home, a twelve-goal cushion in a match that produced 64 goals. The venue now reverses in their favour, which is worth roughly six goals of swing in our calculation and projects a 41-23 scoreline. Sloga Doboj to win the second leg is as close to a formality as the handball card offers.

predictions.competition: BetVictor Northern Ireland Open 2026 - Quarter Finals
predictions.write_up: Mark Williams brings GBP 747,400 of ranking money into a Northern Ireland Open quarter-final against David Gilbert, 34th on the same list with GBP 221,200. Gilbert's twenty centuries this season are the one number that argues the other way and the reason this is priced at -382 rather than shorter. Williams to win, with Gilbert's scoring the risk to respect.

predictions.competition: BetVictor Northern Ireland Open 2026 - Quarter Finals
predictions.write_up: Jak Jones has won GBP 319,300 in ranking money, is fourth on the one-year list with GBP 141,000 and has made sixteen centuries this season; Scott Donaldson sits outside the top 36 and is bounded below GBP 198,500. The margin is narrow enough that this is a 63 per cent call rather than a formality. Jones to win is the pick, at a price inside our focus range.

predictions.competition: BetVictor Northern Ireland Open 2026 - Semi Finals
predictions.write_up: Kyren Wilson reached the Belfast semi-finals as the ninth-ranked player on tour with GBP 716,800 banked, and meets Sam Craigie, who is outside the captured top 36 and therefore under GBP 198,500. The tour's own headline framed this as Wilson and Craigie into the last four; the ranking gap frames the betting. Wilson to win is the selection at 80 per cent, and that figure is a conservative floor.

Mark Selby takes GBP 1,070,500 of ranking money and the biggest one-year list total on tour, GBP 348,350, into a second-round meeting with Jimmy White, who sits outside the published top 36 and therefore below GBP 198,500. Nineteen centuries this season underline the gap. Selby to win is the obvious selection; the price is short because the evidence is one-sided.

Shaun Murphy is seventh on the ranking list with GBP 897,350 and has added GBP 79,350 this season, while Mitchell Mann does not appear in the published top 36, so his ranking money is capped at GBP 198,500 for our purposes. Over a best-of-six-plus format that quality gap usually tells. Murphy to win, with the caveat that a bounded figure makes our price a floor rather than a ceiling.

Zhou Yuelong is 17th on the ranking list with GBP 359,100 against Liam Davies, who is outside the published top 36 and bounded at GBP 198,500. That is a real but modest gap, which is exactly why this sits at -192, inside the price band this desk is focused on. Zhou to win is the selection and the most sensible price on the snooker card.

predictions.competition: India v Zimbabwe ODIs 2026 - Women - 2nd ODI
predictions.write_up: India Women dismissed Zimbabwe Women for 197 in 49.5 overs and knocked the runs off for the loss of a single wicket inside 27.1 overs in the first one-day international - a nine-wicket win with 22.5 overs to spare. Nothing in that contest suggested a close rematch. India Women to win the second ODI is the selection, priced at 80 per cent, which is the cap this desk applies to any single fixture.

Antoine Rozner is 10 under par through 36 holes of the Genesis Championship after rounds of 67 and 65, level with Casey Jarvis and three clear of the quartet on seven under that includes Ryan Fox and Martin Couvra. Among the 25 players captured from the official leaderboard, Rozner prices up as the most likely winner at +271. Treat it as a conditional outright: players outside that group are not priced here.

Kimi Antonelli leads the drivers' standings with 340 points, 102 clear of George Russell, and the official calendar credits him with wins in China, Japan, Miami, Canada and Monaco this season. Among the eight drivers whose points totals were captured, that record makes him the most likely winner of the United States Grand Prix at +288. Qualifying had not run when this was priced, so grid position is not reflected.
